doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Federal pandemic response, masks and Philadelphia riots
summary: She criticizes the federal pandemic response, defends mask wearing, and describes riots, curfew and looting in Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: It’s self-destructive, yeah. Speaking of the government do you have — how do you feel about what your state has done or the federal government?

I think the federal government’s — I mean I am not a Trump supporter in any way, particularly of the Mitch McConnell and all the Senate starting way back from Paul Ryan and Lindsay Graham. I think — I can’t figure out if they — if this is part of a — if the GOP has become a cult or if they all have the same form of mental illness. I mean I really don’t know. I don’t understand what their motives are for some of this behavior, or supporting a president who is clearly a sociopathic narcissist and has severe mental illness, who can’t even speak in sentences, coherent sentences. I don’t understand it. It’s really scary. And I thought the whole response and reaction, and lack of response and barely a reaction from the pandemic was just outrageous and unforgivable with no federal plan or a guideline, or even the simplest — the simplest thing you want from a leader is for somebody to stand in front of you and try to make everything better, or give you focus and hope that we’re going to get through this and this is going to be great. We’ve got none of that on that level. And I think all the governors are of course doing their best, but you know I heard a couple of months ago the governor of North Carolina I believe said, “Oh I didn’t know this was contagious” or something so insane. So not having any guidance from the top and relying on all of our governors, who are also great leaders, it’s been mixed messages all across the board from the leadership. Pennsylvania I think is strict, because it’s so close to New York City. I think tomorrow Pennsylvania is due to go into the Yellow Phase of its reopening but surely everybody will still be wearing a mask. Which I don’t have any problem with. I mean I always thought to myself anytime I got to travel to any Asian country how great and respectful that was that that culture wears a mask if they’re sick because they don’t want to get anybody else sick. And that’s been going on forever. And then for people to be offended and, “You’re taking away my freedom,” it’s like the same thing as no shirt, no shoes, no service. No, wear a mask or get out. Because it’s not about you, it’s about everybody else too. It’s not just about you. So in Philadelphia now, and I’m sure you’re going to go to this topic, is having major riots every night and has an 8:00 curfew. And I live about 25 miles west of Philadelphia. I just moved out of Philadelphia in March. And the city is in chaos right now. And all the major bridges, and like in New York too, in and out of the city, have been closed because of riots. So I don’t know what’s going to happen if we’re going to re-open on Friday or not, combined with all the looting. In Center City Philadelphia one of the major areas by the big Kimmel Performing Arts Center, that’s like the Carnegie Hall of Philly, like from Chase Bank to all the stores and retailers, restaurants, all the windows are smashed out. There’s been crazy looting.
Historians are going to have a field day with 2020.
